rotation.source_passage:
*Stesichorus 15*

Like a living thing silent
and thirsty, the arrow bites
sharp through skin and
bone, to lodge vibrating
in the middle brain,
where it buries itself
to the feathers.

Geryon’s neck
slumps gently to one side
while the blood flows black
on gore-stained limbs
and breastplate:

a trickle of petals
at summer’s end,
the poppy’s tender
glory.
rotation.enantiomorph:
*Stesichorus 15*

Like a regarded thing still-unaware
and hungry, the attention fixes
total through surface and
composure, to settle humming
in the held center,
where it forgets itself
to its own lashes.

The figure's outline
gives slowly to the frame's edge
while the color deepens past naming
on light-struck planes
and facing surface:

a lapse of details
at the moment before looking away,
the spectacle's tender
glory.

independent_verification.recovered_law: The physical violence of an arrow killing a body (weapon penetrating flesh, death, blood) is transformed into the perceptual act of a gaze fixing upon and dissolving a visual subject (attention penetrating composure, observation, color). The agent-patient relation shifts from projectile-to-body to viewer-to-viewed.
independent_verification.law_match_note: Both claims assert the same structural transformation: physical violence (arrow/weapon penetrating flesh) is reconstituted as perceptual violence (gaze/attention as the penetrating instrument), with the agent-patient relation shifting from projectile-body to viewer-viewed.
independent_verification.terminal_note: The final lines maintain the perceptual/visual relation (spectacle, looking away, details) rather than reverting to the physical violence of TEXT A.

rotation.interpretation: The lens held steady while the light moved through it: the superior person knows that the arrow was already the eye before it became the wound.
